source: Public short-read WGS data (NCBI SRA) of clinical and environmental isolates of six Candida species
study_type: Comparative population genomics / convergence GWAS reanalysis of public data
susceptibility_method: Susceptibility data curated from the literature (not tested)
molecular: SNP-based clades; signatures of recent selection (e.g. MRR1a); GWAS for resistance
evidence: "retrieved all publicly available short-read whole-genome sequencing data for pure isolates (that is, clinical and environmental) of six major species"; "isolation source and antifungal drug susceptibility, where available (Fig. 1b and Supplementary Table 1)"
notes: Approx. 2,000 isolates of six species pooled; C. tropicalis counts, sources and countries only in Supplementary Table 1; GWAS was not run for C. tropicalis. No denominators by compartment or country in the main text.

study_type: Experimental microscopy (SEM) study of colony morphology
evidence: "structural analysis of C. tropicalis ATCC 750 colony morphology"; "Side and top views of C. tropicalis colony by SEM"
notes: Uses only a reference strain; no isolates of documented origin and no resistance data.

source: Respiratory samples (tracheal aspirates, BAL) from ventilated COVID-19 ICU patients
identification_method: Not stated (culture on Sabouraud etc. processed with COPAN WASP)
programme_institution: ICU of a teaching hospital in Dendermonde, Belgium
evidence: "The cultures of these samples were processed using COPAN WASP (Walk-away Specimen Processor) on Chocolate Agar, ANC agar, MSA, MacConkey, and Sabouraud medium"; "Of the 51 positive Candida cultures, 65% were C. albicans, 15% C. tropicalis"
notes: No species identification method stated; C. tropicalis only as a percentage (15% of 51 cultures, about 8); no AST.

main_reason: Meets IC1, IC2, IC3, IC5, IC6 and IC7 (species distribution of blood isolates; no AST)
source: Non-duplicate Candida blood isolates (candidaemia) at 25 hospitals
identification_method: Local laboratory methods summarised in Table S2 (supplementary)
programme_institution: Asia Fungal Working Group (AFWG), ISHAM; 25 hospitals
evidence: "Of 1910 blood isolates evaluated, Candida albicans was most frequently isolated (41.3%), followed by Candida tropicalis (25.4%)"; "methods of Candida identification are summarized in Table S2"
notes: n is derived from 25.4% of 1,910 (about 485); per-country counts only in a figure/supplement. Identification methods are in the supplement only. No AST (the authors state that antifungal data were not provided).

source: Fungal isolates from severely burned patients (sputum, burn wounds, blood, pharynx, gastric fluid, catheter, urine, stool)
programme_institution: Burn centre, Yokohama City University Hospital
evidence: "comparison between the C. albicans group (n=38) and non-albicans group (C. tropicalis 18, yeast-like fungi 3), the MIC80 was 5.06 vs 37"; "almost all C. tropicalis strains in our burn unit were resistant to FLCZ"
notes: MIC results are reported for the non-albicans group (18 C. tropicalis + 3 yeast-like fungi) without separating C. tropicalis; only a qualitative statement about the species. Identification method not found.

main_reason: Meets IC1, IC2, IC3, IC5, IC6 and IC7 (colonisation in VLBW neonates; no species-level AST results)
source: Weekly surveillance cultures (colonisation) in preterm VLBW neonates in NICUs
study_type: Secondary analysis of a multicentre RCT
identification_method: Chromogenic agar (Albicans ID) + Vitek Yeast biochemical system
programme_institution: 8 Italian NICUs (fluconazole prophylaxis RCT, Manzoni et al., NEJM 2007)
evidence: "C. tropicalis and C. guilliermondii (1 case each) in the 16 baseline colonised infants"; "C. tropicalis (4 cases)... in the 38 infants with acquired colonisation"; "Colonies were speciated through a miniaturised system of biochemical tests (Vitec Yeast"
notes: C. tropicalis counted by colonised infant (1 baseline + 4 acquired). Fluconazole was tested, but results are not reported by species, so IC4 is not met. Same RCT cohort as the NEJM 2007 trial (EC12).

main_reason: Meets IC1, IC2, IC3, IC5, IC6 and IC7 (endophytic C. tropicalis from edible tubers; no AST)
source: Endophytic fungi from tiger nut (Cyperus esculentus) tubers bought at markets (Ile-Ife, Ado-Ekiti, Osogbo)
evidence: "TGY4 Candida tropicalis isolate ZA030 (JN606259.1) 99.80 ... MZ452357"; "the endophytic fungi isolated were Saccharomyces cerevisiae and Candida tropicalis"
notes: Single isolate from a cultivated crop product (assigned to C3). Market-purchased tubers, so the farm of origin is unknown. No susceptibility testing.

main_reason: Meets all IC; C. tropicalis resistance with denominators per antifungal and CLSI M60
source: Blood isolates from candidaemia episodes (all wards, incl. ICU and haemato-oncology)
identification_method: CHROMagar Candida + API ID 32 C (2005-2012); MALDI-TOF VITEK MS (from 2012)
standard_version: CLSI M60 (2017) breakpoints; CLSI M59 (2018) ECVs
evidence: "C. tropicalis (n = 168, 18 %)"; Table 1: "Candida tropicalis 8/168 (4.8%) 13/165 (8%) 12/164 (7.4%) 0/166 (0%)"; "interpreted according to the Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute (CLSI) M60 breakpoints"
notes: Per-antifungal denominators in Table 1 (168/165/164/166); the column-to-drug mapping needs to be confirmed at extraction. Resistant was defined as non-susceptible.

source: Clinical isolates from the female reproductive tract (candidal dysbiosis) + ATCC reference strains
study_type: Experimental in vitro biofilm chronobiology study
identification_method: Phenotypic (colony morphology, chlamydospores, germ tube, assimilation, disc diffusion)
evidence: "Объектом исследования служили 17 изолятов С. albicans, C. tropicalis и C. krusei, выделенные из женского репродуктивного тракта"; control ATCC C. tropicalis 750
notes: 17 isolates of three species with no C. tropicalis count; only biofilm outcomes; no resistance profile.

main_reason: Meets general rule; in-house breakpoints without a standard document (IC8 not met)
source: Clinical specimens (respiratory, gastrointestinal, urinary) from oncology and non-oncology patients
identification_method: Standard macroscopic, microscopic and biochemical methods
standard_version: Not a standard; in-house breakpoints (AMB R >=2 ug/ml; nystatin R >=16 ug/ml)
molecular: Sterol (ergosterol) UV spectral analysis of resistant isolates
evidence: Table 1: "C. tropicalis 197 68 100 18"; Table 2: "C. tropicalis 3 (0.4) 1 (1.4)"; "resistance was defined as a minimal inhibitory concentration of greater than or equal to 2 micrograms/ml for amphotericin B and greater than or equal to 16 micrograms/ml for nystatin"
notes: 197 non-oncology + 100 oncology C. tropicalis isolates; 3 resistant isolates from one oncology patient. Exact years are not stated in the excerpt.
